note: CAC-GP-1.8. The source of truth for what is a guard. Discovery used to glob four filename patterns, which let eight real guards escape — seven copies of decisions-render.sh plus ai-register/exposure.sh, none of them ever mutation-tested, and the GP-1.7 registry check filtered through the same list so it confirmed its own blind spot (BL-101). Filename convention could never have caught both: seven shared a name no convention anticipated, and the eighth shared nothing with anything. This file classifies EVERY skills/*/evals/*.sh. A script in none of these lists fails the run — that is the whole point, and it is why the registry lists non-guards too.

roles.guard: Proved under CAC-GP-1. Must have skills/<skill>/evals/guard-proofs/<name>.json with one mutation per half.
roles.candidate: Guard-shaped by the standard's own definition, not yet enrolled because it has no registered mutation. Counted and printed on every run so the number is visible rather than implied. Enrolment is BL-99.
roles.not-a-guard: Asserts what the product DOES, or checks the environment. Not a defect-cannot-occur property.

scripts.reason: Behavioural suite over the real CLI. Asserts what the engine DOES, not a defect it forbids.

PERMANENT candidate. the maintainer's decision, 2026-08-09, after ten of the eleven candidates enrolled. Not a backlog entry and not a guard: a third answer that is true.

No mutation defeats it, and the reason is the point. The suite runs an A/B holding every declared fact constant and moving only revenue and headcount, asserting the applicability objects come back byte-identical. To defeat it a mutation must make A and B DIFFER — but `applies(profile, question_sets, subject)` never receives the store, so revenue and headcount are STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE from the function that decides scope. The separation this suite protects is enforced by the call signature, not by convention.

A mutation would have to widen that signature first, which is a design change and not a proof. Enrolling it under CAC-GP-1 would mean registering a mutation that trips an adjacent check and calling the guard proved — the exact failure GP-1.9 exists for.

If `applies()` ever gains access to the store, this row must be revisited: the defect becomes expressible, and a mutation becomes both possible and required.
